1.q: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah
1.note: The word “All” is a generalization. Some people may not have wanted him to be king. Alternate translation: [The people of Judah took the 16 year-old Uzziah and made him king after his father, Amaziah]

2.q: It was he who rebuilt Elath
2.note: Uzziah did not do this alone. Alternate translation: [It was he who ordered Elath to be rebuilt] or [It was he who supervised the rebuilding of Elath]
“returned it to Judah.” This means that his army captured the city so that now it belonged to Judah again.
This is a polite way to say he died.

4.q: what was right in the eyes of Yahweh
4.note: The eyes represent seeing, and seeing represents thoughts or judgment. See how you translated a similar phrase in 2 Chronicles 14:2. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh judges to be right] or [what Yahweh considers to be right]

4.q: following the example of his father, Amaziah, in everything
4.note: This implies that his father had done what was right in God’s eyes. Alternate translation: [just as his father, Amaziah, had done]
This is a generalization. Alternate translation: [in the same way]

5.q: He set himself to seek God
5.note: Here “set himself” is a metaphor for being determined to do something. Seeking God represents choosing to know, worship, and obey him. Alternate translation: [He was determined to obey God]
Here “the days of Zechariah” is a metonym referring to the time period during which Zechariah was priest. Alternate translation: [when Zechariah was priest]

5.q: As long as he sought Yahweh
5.note: Alternate translation: [During the whole time that he sought Yahweh]
Seeking Yahweh represents choosing to know, worship, and obey him. Alternate translation: [chose to obey Yahweh]

6.q: Uzziah went out and fought against the Philistines
6.note: Here “Uzziah” represents himself and his army that he led. Alternate translation: [Uzziah led his army out to fight against the Philistines] or [Uzziah and his army went out and fought against the Philistines]

6.q: He broke down … he built cities
6.note: Here the pronouns “He” and “him” represent Uzziah and his army. Alternate translation: [Uzziah and his army broke down … they built cities]
This was a town in northern Judah.
Alternate translation: [the country surrounding Ashdod] or [near Ashdod]

7.note: Here the pronouns “He” and “him” represent Uzziah and his army. Alternate translation: [God helped them]
This was a town in Arabia.
This is likely people who moved to that area from the kingdom of Maon near Mount Seir.

8.q: his fame spread, even to the entrance of Egypt
8.note: His fame spreading is a metaphor for people in various places learning about him. Alternate translation: [people who lived even as far away as the border of Egypt learned about the things he was doing]

9.note: Here “Uzziah” represents the workers he had commanded to build the towers. Alternate translation: [Uzziah had his workers build towers] or [Uzziah’s workers built towers]

10.q: He built watchtowers … and dug many cisterns
10.note: Uzziah commanded his workers, and they did these things. Alternate translation: [He had his workers build watchtowers … and dig many cisterns] or [They built watchtowers … and dug many cisterns]

10.q: he had much cattle … He had farmers … he loved farming

11.note: These are the names of men.

12.q: the leaders of the families who led the mighty men
12.note: Alternate translation: [the family leaders who led the mighty men]

13.q: Under their hand was an army
13.note: Here “their hand” represents their authority. Alternate translation: [Under their authority was an army] or [They commanded an army]

14.note: A helmet is a protective head covering.
This is a covering for the body made of metal links or chains.

15.q: he built machines that were designed by skillful men
15.note: Here “he built machines” represents Uzziah commanding his workers to build them. Alternate translation: [his workers built machines that were designed by skillful men]
These were the corners of the city walls where soldiers could fight from.
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God greatly helped him]

16.note: Here the heart being lifted up represents pride. Alternate translation: [he became proud]

17.q: with him eighty priests of Yahweh, who were brave men
17.note: The verb “went” is understood from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: [with him went eighty priests of Yahweh, who were brave men] or [eighty priests of Yahweh, who were brave men, went with him]

18.q: It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to Yahweh
18.note: Alternate translation: [It is not right for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to Yahweh] or [Uzziah, you do not have the right to burn incense to Yahweh]
Here “sons” represents descendants. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Aaron]

18.q: who are consecrated to burn incense
18.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whom God has consecrated to burn incense] or [whom God has chosen to burn incense]

19.note: This is a special pan or bowl used for burning incense.

20.note: The word “behold” here shows that the priests were surprised by what they saw.

20.q: They quickly drove him out of there
20.note: Alternate translation: [They quickly forced him out of there] or [They quickly made him leave]
This speaks of Yahweh making him sick as if Yahweh had hit him. Alternate translation: [Yahweh had made him ill]

21.q: to the day of his death
21.note: Alternate translation: [until he died] or [the rest of his life]
This indicates that he lived away from other houses and other people.

21.q: he was cut off from the house of Yahweh
21.note: Here being “cut off” from Yahweh’s house represents being excluded from the temple. Alternate translation: [he was excluded from the house of Yahweh] or [he was not allowed to go to the temple]

21.q: Jotham, his son, was over the king’s house
21.note: Here being over something represents having responsibility or authority for it. Alternate translation: [Jotham, his son, was responsible for the king’s house] or [Jotham, his son, was in charge of the palace]
This refers to the king’s palace, which the king was no longer living in.

22.q: The other matters concerning Uzziah, from first to last, were recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz
22.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [As for the other matters concerning Uzziah, from first to last, the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz recorded them]
This phrase represents the whole time of Uzziah’s reign. Alternate translation: [from the beginning of his reign to the end of his reign]
This is the name of a man.

23.q: So Uzziah slept with his ancestors
23.note: This is polite way to say that he died. Alternate translation: [So Uzziah died]

23.q: they buried him with his ancestors
23.note: Alternate translation: [the people buried him near his ancestors] or [they buried him where his ancestors were buried]

23.q: Jotham, his son, became king in his place
23.note: Alternate translation: [Jotham, his son, became king after Uzziah]
